 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioner-accused No.1 is before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail in Crime No.26/2024 of Halasurgate Police Station, pending on the file of learned III Additional CMM Court,
Nrupathunga Road, Bengaluru City, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 120B,
409, 419, 420, 468 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant- Sri.Vijayaraghava Marathe.

sentences.text: 2. Heard Sri.Prasanna Kumar P., learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.Rahul Rai K., learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.

Perused the materials on record.
3.

In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"
NC: 2024:KHC:20595 My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 4.
The petitioner arrayed as accused No.1 is seeking grant of anticipatory bail on apprehension of being arrested.

The informant lodged the first information against accused Nos.1 to 3 alleging that without calling any tender, accused No.1 was permitted to collect parking charges by accused No.3 and they have committed the offence as stated above.
It is not in dispute that accused Nos.2 and 3 are already granted anticipatory bail.

5. My attention was drawn by the learned counsel for the petitioner to the letter dated 23.01.2024 addressed by the Deputy Commissioner to the Investigating Officer, wherein, he has given an explanation as to why accused No.1 was permitted to manage the parking area and collect the parking charges.
It is stated that accused No.1 had taken the parking area on lease during 2018-19.
During COVID-19 due to lockdown, no fresh tender was called.

Later, the tender process has started,
but in the meantime to manage the parking area, accused No.1 was permitted to collect the parking fees and a NC: 2024:KHC:20595 sum of `1,31,500/- being monthly rent is being paid by accused No.1.

6. Considering the explanation offered by the Deputy Commissioner, I am of the opinion that the petitioner may be granted anticipatory bail subject to conditions, which will take care of the interest of the prosecution.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.
The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in the event of his arrest in Crime No.26/2024 of Halasurgate Police Station.

The petitioner is directed to appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of this order and on his appearance, the Investigating Officer shall enlarge him on bail subject to the following conditions:-
a.

The petitioner shall furnish the bond in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) NC: 2024:KHC:20595 with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer; b. The petitioner shall not commit any offences; c.
The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer or the court as and when required; and d.
The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses.
On furnishing the sureties by the petitioner, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to verify the correctness of the address and authenticity of the documents furnished by him.
On satisfaction of the said documents, he may proceed to accept the sureties within a reasonable time.
